blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Enterprise supply chain risk management, at senior level, is the discipline of looking at the whole chain through the lens of 'what could seriously hurt this company?' and preparing, honestly, for the versions of the future that would hurt most. It is not paranoia. It is the quiet, rational acceptance that the chain will be tested, and that the teams who have rehearsed recover faster than those who have not.

The senior leader focuses on correlation. Individual risks can be insured, hedged, or lived with. It is the scenarios where several risks fire together that break companies. A currency move alongside a key supplier failure alongside a regulatory change in the destination country is not a hypothetical — it is the kind of combination that has ended companies that looked healthy the month before.

The discipline is to imagine, specifically, the bad quarters that could happen, to size the company's buffers against them, and to rehearse the responses in conversation so they are not invented in a panic. Companies that do this live through things that kill their less-prepared competitors — usually without anyone outside noticing.

items.q: According to the text, what is enterprise supply chain risk management NOT?
items.why: "It is not paranoia. It is the quiet, rational acceptance that the chain will be tested."

items.q: What, according to the text, is most likely to break companies?
options: The cost of hedging currency exposure
Scenarios where several risks fire together
items.why: "It is the scenarios where several risks fire together that break companies."

items.q: Why does the text say rehearsed responses matter?
options: So they replace the need for buffers
So they can be insured more cheaply
So they are not invented in a panic
items.why: "to rehearse the responses in conversation so they are not invented in a panic."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Buffers should be sized against specific bad quarters.
Correlated risks deserve more attention than isolated ones.
A company that looks healthy is therefore safe.
items.why: Inferência: o texto cita empresas que "looked healthy the month before" e ainda assim quebraram — aparência de saúde não é segurança.

items.q: The phrase "usually without anyone outside noticing" suggests that…
options: good risk management works invisibly, absorbing shocks before they surface
regulators rarely audit the supply chain
items.why: Inferência: a preparação faz a empresa atravessar o choque sem que o mercado perceba — o sucesso é justamente a ausência de crise visível.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte apresentando o stress test ao comitê executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. What you have on the screen is not a list of things I am worried about individually. Each of these risks, on its own, we can handle — we insure the freight, we hedge the currency, we hold credit lines against the supplier. Taken one at a time, none of them keeps me awake.

What I have modelled instead is the corner of the table where three of them arrive in the same quarter. Column four is the one I would ask you to look at. A sharp move in the real, at the same time as our second-largest origin supplier going offline, at the same time as the new export licensing rule in the destination market. Individually, survivable. Together, our buffers are gone by week six, and we are financing the gap on terms we would not choose.

Now, I am not saying this combination is likely. I am saying it is not hypothetical, and that two of our peers have already lived a milder version of it. So my recommendation is simple: we hold a deeper buffer against this scenario, and we rehearse the first ten days as a committee, on paper, before we ever do it for real.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Charlotte describe each risk taken individually?
options: The main reason she loses sleep
items.why: "Each of these risks, on its own, we can handle… none of them keeps me awake."

items.q: What does column four of the model represent?
options: Three risks arriving in the same quarter
items.why: "the corner of the table where three of them arrive in the same quarter. Column four is the one I would ask you to look at."

items.q: In the column-four scenario, what happens to the company's buffers?
options: They are gone by week six
items.why: "our buffers are gone by week six, and we are financing the gap on terms we would not choose."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply by saying the combination is "not hypothetical"?
options: It has been ruled out by the board
It is too rare to plan for
It has already occurred, in a milder form, to comparable companies
It is certain to happen next quarter
items.why: Inferência: ela reforça que "two of our peers have already lived a milder version of it" — não é fantasia, tem precedente real.

items.q: What is the underlying purpose of Charlotte's recommendation to rehearse the first ten days?
options: To reduce the cost of insurance premiums
To avoid improvising the response under pressure
To demonstrate the model to regulators
To replace the need for a deeper buffer
items.why: Inferência: ensaiar "on paper, before we ever have to do it for real" existe para que a resposta não seja inventada no pânico.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We assess the whole chain through the lens of what could seriously hurt the company." Here, a lens is…
options: a perspective through which something is examined
items.why: Lens (figurado) = a perspectiva ou o enfoque pelo qual se olha algo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Preparing for a plausible bad quarter is prudence, not ___."
items.why: Paranoia = medo irracional; o texto opõe a preparação racional à paranoia.

items.q: "It is the quiet, rational acceptance that the chain will be tested." This phrase describes…
items.why: Rational acceptance = aceitar com serenidade e razão que o choque virá, sem negá-lo nem entrar em pânico.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ our currency exposure so that a sharp move in the real does not sink the quarter."
items.why: To hedge = fazer hedge, proteger-se contra a variação de preço ou câmbio.

items.q: "Their cash buffer was exhausted by week six." A buffer is…
options: a reserve that absorbs a shock
items.why: Buffer = reserva/folga que absorve o impacto antes que ele atinja a operação.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de comitê de risco. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The risk committee still has to sign off on the deeper buffer." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two members pushed back on the size of the reserve." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's not overreact to one bad month; it won't move the needle on our overall exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We agreed to rehearse the response, but the team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "When the licensing rule hit, we had to fall back on our secondary supplier." To fall back on means to…
options: turn to it as a reserve option
items.why: Fall back on = recorrer a algo como alternativa de reserva quando a opção principal falha.
